name: AWS Neuron: neuroncc compilation, NEFF format, and auto-casting
arithmetic_intensity: The Neuron Graph Compiler (neuronx-cc) transforms ML models from TensorFlow/MXNet/PyTorch/XLA HLO into NEFF (Neuron Executable File Format). It auto-casts FP32 operations to BF16 by default for optimal performance. Supports optimization levels 1-3 (compilation time vs runtime performance). Model-specific optimizations for Transformer and U-Net architectures. Logical NeuronCore sharding for distributed inference. The compiler is invoked transparently through framework plugins.
scales_with: optimization_level (1-3, higher = better runtime but longer compile)
precision (FP32->BF16 auto-cast, or FP8 for higher throughput)
workarounds: Use optimization level 3 for production (best runtime performance)
Use FP8 (cFP8) on Inferentia2/Trainium2 for 2x throughput vs FP16
Configure logical NeuronCore sharding for multi-chip inference
notes: The compilation model is similar to TPU's XLA but with more user control. The auto-casting path is the key productivity feature: 'AWS Neuron takes high-precision FP32 models and automatically casts them to lower-precision data types while optimizing accuracy and performance.' This removes the need for lower-precision retraining. The NEFF format is the deployment artifact — compiled once, loaded by the runtime. For inference, the tradeoff is optimization level (compile time vs runtime performance) and precision (FP8 vs BF16 vs FP16).
